sources.title: Michael Aung-Thwin, Myanmar in the Fifteenth Century
sources.note: University of Hawaii Press scholarly overview of the First Pegu and Ava kingdoms, chronology and downstream commercial setting.

sources.title: Tin Tin Win, A Study on the Causes of the Disintegration of Hanthawaddy Kingdom
sources.note: Myanmar Academy of Arts and Science study of the 1539 conquest, Tabinshwehti, Bayinnaung, Nanda and political collapse.

sources.title: Michael Aung-Thwin, A tale of two kingdoms
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of downstream commercial Pegu, upstream agrarian Ava and the limits of a simple ethnic-war narrative.

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, Ethnic Hatred and Universal Benevolence
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of migration, rice expansion, trade, literacy limits, mixed Toungoo court, 1539 conquest and 1590s collapse.

sources.title: Emmanuel Guillon, Les villes du Pegou aux XIVe et XVe siecles
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of Lower Myanmar geography, strong monsoons, estuaries, ports, cities and cultural development.

sources.title: Anne M. Blackburn, Buddhist-Inflected Sovereignties across the Indian Ocean
sources.note: University of Hawaii Press study of Shin Sawbu, Dhammaceti, delta sovereignty, Pali-Mon inscriptions and Sri Lankan connections.

sources.title: H. L. Shorto, The Kyaikmaraw Inscriptions
sources.note: Peer-reviewed edition identifying Shin Sawbu's 1455 land dedication as the earliest dated Middle Mon inscription.

sources.title: Taw Sein Ko, The Kalyani Inscriptions of King Dhammaceti
sources.note: Public-domain Archaeological Survey text and translation of the 1476 Pali and Mon inscriptions at Pegu.

sources.title: Ei Ei Zaw, Religious Contribution of Hanthawaddy Period
sources.note: Yangon University of Education study of royal Buddhist patronage, pagoda repair and literary activity from 1369 to 1453.

sources.title: Mabel Haynes Bode, The Pali Literature of Burma
sources.note: Scholarly survey of Pali works, monastic learning and Dhammaceti's Sri Lankan ordination mission.

sources.title: Luis Filipe Thomaz, Les premiers voyages portugais a Pasai et a Pegou
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of the first Portuguese voyages to Pegu from 1512 to 1520 and their commercial context.

sources.title: Hieronimo di Santo Stefano, Account of the Journey to Pegu
sources.note: SOAS-hosted translation of a Genoese merchant account describing Pegu in 1495 to 1496, including court and elephant claims.

sources.title: Ralph Fitch, England's Pioneer to India and Burma
sources.note: Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts scan of Fitch's 1586 to 1587 eyewitness account of waterways, homes, warehouses, trade and monastic customs.

sources.title: Cesare Federici, Account of Pegu
sources.note: SOAS-edited primary account of Pegu in the 1560s, used cautiously for city form, goods, dress and outsider observation.

sources.title: NUS Museum, From the Ashes: Reviving Myanmar Celadon Ceramics
sources.note: National University of Singapore catalogue on fifteenth and sixteenth-century Twante kilns, ceramic technology, forms and overseas finds.

sources.title: Asia Society, Buddhist Art of Myanmar
sources.note: Museum catalogue with scholarly entries on Lower Myanmar Buddhist art, royal patronage, inscriptions and trade.

sources.title: Bago Region Government, Kanbawzathadi Palace
sources.note: Official site history and archaeological description of Bayinnaung's Hanthawaddy palace and its surviving excavated evidence.

sources.title: UNESCO tentative list, Mon cities: Bago and Hanthawaddy
sources.note: Myanmar Department of Archaeology nomination recording ancient Mon urban sites and excavation of the palace area.

sources.title: Tin Tin Win, History of Hanthawaddy Kingdom, 1539 to 1599
sources.note: University of Yangon dissertation record for First Toungoo rule from Pegu, administration, court, war and the 1599 ending.

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, The transfer of the Burmese capital from Pegu to Ava
sources.note: Peer-reviewed correction of oversimplified claims about the 1635 move from Pegu to Ava and indigenous naming of capitals.

sources.title: Myanmar Department of Traditional Medicine, Milestones of Traditional Medicine
sources.note: Official historical survey of Myanmar medical traditions, categories and evidence, used only as broad background with local limits.

sources.title: Myanmar International TV, Hanthawady ancient city archaeology
sources.note: Report quoting the Bago Department of Archaeology on the excavated city wall, water, mud and dry moats and their defensive roles.

sources.title: Michael Aung-Thwin, Pagan: The Origins of Modern Burma, justice and hierarchy
sources.note: University of Hawaii Press chapter on premodern Myanmar hierarchy, Buddhist law and appeals, used as labeled institutional background.

sources.title: Thida, Mon Alphabets and Changing Period
sources.note: Myanmar Academy of Arts and Science overview of the Wareru line, Pegu capital, 1539 conquest, Toungoo capital phase and Mon literary continuity.

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, Ethnic Politics in Eighteenth-Century Burma
sources.note: Peer-reviewed periodization distinguishing First Toungoo at Pegu from Restored Toungoo usually centered at Ava.

sources.title: Gasparo Balbi, Voyage to Pegu and Observations There
sources.note: SOAS Bulletin edition of a 1583 traveler account describing dangerous tides, delta pilots, river movement and Pegu.

sources.title: NUS Southeast Asian Studies, From the Ashes exhibition
sources.note: National University of Singapore overview of fifteenth-century Twante ceramics and their long-distance distribution.

sources.title: Royal Asiatic Society review, Inscriptions of the Kalyanisima at Pegu
sources.note: Scholarly bibliographic record for the Pali and Mon stone inscriptions of Dhammaceti at Pegu.

proposedOverrides.summary: A maritime Lower Myanmar kingdom whose Pegu capital later served a different Toungoo empire, while the atlas merges those phases from 1492 to 1650.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported id pegu is indexed circa 1492 to 1650 and was missing both a card and researched override at initial audit.
The historical Hanthawaddy polity began in 1287, made Pegu its capital later, fell to Toungoo in 1539 and briefly revived from 1550 to 1552.
Pegu then served as the First Toungoo capital. That city continuity is not a continuous independent Hanthawaddy kingdom through 1650.
No appliesTo alias is added. The separately indexed burmese-kingdoms, ava, pagan-1279, mon-state, arakan, ayutthaya and sukhothai records remain untouched.
The 1492 and 1500 target polygons have 33 positions; the 1530 and 1600 polygons are identical 49-position geometries.
The 1530 and 1600 geometry includes tested Mawlamyine, Hinthada and Dawei but excludes Pyay and Taungoo, which remain with burmese-kingdoms.
The card uses periods for the exact 1492 to 1650 map window and marks the changing political identity inside that imported coverage.
The structured ending records the final 1552 end of independent Hanthawaddy after its brief revival, with burmese-kingdoms as atlas-facing territorial successor.
